---
title: "Metric overview"
description: "Choose a metric from the relationship your embedding should preserve."
---

This package provides several ways to evaluate the performance of an
embedding. Start with the relationship you want to check.

## Choosing a Starting Metric

| User question | Reasonable starting metric | Decision supported by the result |
|---|---|---|
| Are the same nearby observations retained? | `nn_preservation()` | Whether local-neighborhood identity is preserved well enough for the intended use. |
| Do dense and sparse regions keep their relative local scale? | `local_radius_correlation()` | Whether scale distortion needs attention even when neighbor identities look acceptable. |
| Are broad distance orderings retained? | `random_triplet_accuracy()` | Whether the embedding preserves enough global ordering for the intended use. |
| Do known labels remain retrievable? | `roc_auc()` or `pr_auc()` | Whether same-label observations rank ahead of other labels in the embedding. |
| Did a neighborhood keep its members but change shape? | `local_procrustes()` | Inspect the matched points in the [Swiss-roll patch](reference-geometry.html#compare-local-shape-after-alignment). |
| Did a gap open between groups? | `gap_index()` | Locate the triangle spanning the [gap between three digits](mnist-pca-umap.html#inspect-the-gaps-between-digits). |
| Does a visible island represent a coherent group in the reference? | `steadiness_cohesiveness()` | Check [label-free groups in the MNIST audit](mnist-pca-umap.html#check-groups-without-digit-labels) in both directions. |
| Did a class pair become easier to retrieve while its geometry changed? | Pairwise AUC, label trustworthiness and continuity, and CADI | Compare retrieval, centroid separation, and [the spread of 5s seen from 3s](mnist-pca-umap.html#compare-angular-spread-from-each-digit). |

## Which metrics work on large datasets?

Around **5,000 observations**, check the memory budget before constructing a distance matrix.
One dense `N` by `N` double matrix takes `8 * N^2` bytes for its entries. At 5,000 rows, budget
191 MiB for one space, 381.5 MiB for a reference and one embedding, or 572 MiB for a reference
and two embeddings. A single matrix grows from 7.6 MiB at 1,000 rows to 763 MiB at 10,000 and
26.8 GiB at 60,000. Allow additional memory for coordinates, copies and working storage. The
practical limit depends on which metric you run and how much memory is available.

| What you want to check | Recommended approach for large data | What determines the cost |
|---|---|---|
| Global distances and ordering | Start with `random_pair_distance_correlation()`, `random_pair_distance_emd()`, `random_pair_distance_stress()`, `random_pair_distance_band_profile()` or `random_triplet_accuracy()` on the full coordinates. Reuse the sampled pairs or triplets across embeddings. | Only sampled distances are evaluated. `n_pairs` is a total count. For triplet accuracy, `n_triplets` is a count **per observation**. Check how many sampled pairs fall in the narrowest band. |
| Neighbor overlap, local radius or reciprocal neighbors | Use `nn_preservation()`, `nbr_pres_knn()`, `local_radius_correlation()` or `mutual_neighbor_correlation()` with existing neighbor graphs. When building graphs, consider approximate search and spot-check its recall. | A graph holding `k` neighbors per row has `N * k` entries. Brute-force search still evaluates all pairs. Radius comparisons also need neighbor distances. |
| Exact neighborhood ranks | For Euclidean coordinates, use `exact_rank_profiles()` with selected `query_rows` and a few `k` values. | Each query ranks the full pool. Scoring every query still requires quadratic distance work, even though the per-query workspace is linear in `N`. |
| Label separation or angular spread | Use `label_trustworthiness_continuity()` for centroid separation or `class_angular_distortion_index()` for angles. | The first visits every pair of classes. The second works on sampled triplets, with `n_triplets` a **total** count. Neither needs all observation-pair distances. |
| Local shape or empty regions | Reuse a reference neighbor graph for `local_procrustes()`. Use `gap_index()` for gaps in a 2D map. | Procrustes fits one small alignment per row. Gap Index triangulates the embedding and evaluates the triangle edges. Both avoid a dense distance matrix. |
| Changes in shared neighbors | Use `neighbor_dissimilarity()` when the identities of the affected pairs matter. | Its sparse graph product can approach `N^2` entries when many rows share a popular neighbor. This also affects the scalar score. |

**When to use a smaller dataset.** `nbr_pres()`, `trustworthiness()`, `continuity()`, `rnx_auc()`,
`rnx_curve()`, `pointwise_rank_preservation()` and `pointwise_rnx()` each take **two dense distance
matrices**. `roc_auc()`, `pr_auc()` and `class_pair_auc()` take **one per space**. If you need AUC
for just two classes, select those classes before computing distances. If the full matrices exceed
your budget, use the same representative subset in every space and report the candidate pool size.

For `steadiness_cohesiveness()`, start with a representative subset. It takes coordinates, then
builds dense distance and similarity matrices and repeatedly clusters sampled groups.
Asking for pointwise scores adds more square matrices. Fewer iterations save CPU while the dense
allocations remain. The MNIST workflow ran exact coordinate ranks for all 5,000 images and used
1,000 for the group comparison.
[MNIST group audit](mnist-pca-umap.html#check-groups-without-digit-labels)

### Sample queries when the full neighbor pool matters

To estimate rank preservation for the full dataset, sample the **queries** and keep every row of
the reference and embeddings. With `x` and `maps` from the MNIST workflow, these 500 queries each
rank the other 4,999 images. The mean gives each sampled query equal weight.

```{r overview-sample-queries, eval=FALSE}
set.seed(42)
queries <- sample.int(nrow(x), 500)
profiles <- exact_rank_profiles(x, maps, k = 15, query_rows = queries)
vapply(profiles, function(p) mean(p$trustworthiness[, 1]), numeric(1))
```

Subsetting the coordinate matrices also removes candidates and changes what the ranks mean. On
the same MNIST queries at `k = 100`, 7s retained neighbors better than 0s in the 1,000-image pool,
while 0s did better in the 5,000-image pool. At `k = 500` in the larger pool, 7s led again. Report
the number of queries, the size of the candidate pool and `k`.
[Full-pool MNIST comparison](mnist-pca-umap.html#expand-the-candidate-pool-to-all-5000-images)

## Local Neighborhood Preservation

`nbr_pres()` compares neighborhoods from exact distance matrices.
`nn_preservation()` and `nbr_pres_knn()` compare nearest-neighbor graphs.

`trustworthiness()` and `continuity()` score misplaced neighbors by their ranks.
`rnx_auc()` summarizes rank-based neighborhood agreement over many neighborhood sizes, while
`rnx_curve()` retains the individual scales. `pointwise_rnx()` gives the comparison per observation.

To check whether the closest neighbors retain their order, use `exact_rank_profiles()` with
`mrre = TRUE`. Compare input and output mean relative rank error at the same `k`. Smaller values
indicate better preservation.
[Worked example](local-preservation.html#can-the-same-neighbors-come-back-in-a-different-order)

See the [local preservation](local-preservation.html) article for examples and
related local diagnostics.

## Local Scale Preservation

Neighbor identity does not say whether dense and sparse regions keep their
relative scale. `local_radius_correlation()` compares the local radius around
each observation in the input data and output embedding, using either the
distance to the `k`th neighbor or the mean distance to the first `k` neighbors.

## Local Shape Preservation

`local_procrustes()` checks how much the same reference neighborhood changes shape after
rigid alignment. It can find distortions even when all members stay together.

## Regional Area Distortion

`gap_index()` locates expansion and compression in the empty triangles of a 2D embedding.
[MNIST example](mnist-pca-umap.html#inspect-the-gaps-between-digits)

## Local Graph Diagnostics

`mutual_neighbor_correlation()` compares the mutual-neighbor count pattern in
the input and output nearest-neighbor graphs. It asks whether points with many
or few reciprocal nearest-neighbor relationships in the input graph have
similar counts in the output graph.

Use `neighbor_dissimilarity()` when the question is which pairs of observations gain or lose
shared neighbors. [Graph comparison](local-preservation.html#which-pairs-share-the-same-neighbors)

## Global Distance Preservation

`quadra` also contains random triplet and random pair distance methods for
global structure preservation:

* `random_triplet_accuracy()` checks whether sampled distance orderings are
preserved.
* `random_pair_distance_correlation()` measures Pearson or Spearman correlation
between sampled input and output distances.
* `random_pair_distance_emd()` compares sampled distance distributions using
Earth Mover's Distance.
* `random_pair_distance_stress()` compares matched sampled distances with a
root mean squared difference.

For these metrics, `Xin` and `metric_in` define the reference geometry.

The [identity-permutation example](global-preservation.html#identical-scatterplots-different-point-identities)
shows which metrics notice when the same plotted positions belong to different observations.
Use [distance bands](distance-band-fidelity.html) to compare ordering and fitted-scale stress
from nearby input pairs through the entire pair sample.

## Input and Ordering Conventions

Sampled pair and triplet metrics require dense, finite inputs; graph metrics
accept the sparse inputs supported by `rnndescent`.

`nbr_pres()` includes boundary ties, exact-rank metrics break ties by column
order, and supplied-graph metrics use their stored order.

Euclidean and squared Euclidean induce the same ordering but different
magnitudes. This distinction affects Pearson correlation, EMD, stress, and
local-scale summaries, but not neighbor, triplet, or Spearman ordering.

## Label Retrieval

`roc_auc()` and `pr_auc()` rank other observations by distance from each query
and treat matching labels as relevant. They require the
[PRROC package](https://cran.r-project.org/package=PRROC).

`label_trustworthiness_continuity()` compares each class pair's centroid separation with
its separation in the input. `class_angular_distortion_index()` measures changes in the
angles that one class subtends from points in another.

See the [label retrieval](label-retrieval.html) article for examples and return
value details.
